decision: FENCE_QUALIFIED_WITHIN_INSTRUMENTED_SCOPE; NOT qualified for general virtio-blk or hardware
scope: isolated instrumented QEMU 11.1.2 TCG backend, legacy PCI virtio-blk, split queue 0, static pinned guest RAM, request never submitted to the block backend

properties.evidence: guest ADMISSION_CLOSED precedes RESET_REQUESTED in every async run
RequestId retained in coordinator inventory and in the terminal outcome
CAS owner; RESET_OWNER_CONTESTED on a distinct CPU at 2 and 4 CPUs
device RESET_ACKNOWLEDGED plus guest status-zero readback
MAPPING_RELEASED after WORKER_JOINED and before RESET_ACKNOWLEDGED
no access event after acknowledgment in the positive model; the negative model is detected
the held request is never submitted; blk_drain() is not exercised
static pinned RAM only; no hot-unplug, migration or reuse
no physical device, no IOMMU, no bus-level observation
the held write was never submitted and no flush was issued

normative_vs_implementation.normative: VirtIO 1.4 CS01 whole-device reset and queue-interaction contract; conditional on a conforming device and platform
normative_vs_implementation.implementation: QEMU 11.1.2: address_space_map pins the MemoryRegion; blk_drain covers only the block layer; device-private work must be joined by the device
normative_vs_implementation.experimental: 12 positive and 6 negative native runs on 1/2/4 CPUs and both cache modes

critical_distinction: A completed reset is not by itself proof that every host callback and mapping has been retired, and a quiescent emulator callback is not proof of hardware DMA fencing. Only the first claim is established here, and only for the instrumented backend.

fail_stop.bounded_failure: QUIESCE_TIMEOUT_BOUNDED and DrainOutcome::Bounded exist and are tested
